counterexample: Consider a DAG with vertices V={1, 2, 3} and edges E={(1,2), (2,3), (1,3)}. The shortest path from 1 to 3 has length 1 (the edge (1,3)), but there is an intermediate vertex 2 with paths 1->2 and 2->3. Thus, (1,3) is not in R, refuting the claim in step 0024 that a shortest path of length 1 implies no intermediate vertices exist.
